content: 1. When co-administered with cannabidiol, carbamazepine reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Esomeprazole decreases the level or effect of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 3. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction is relevant only to the oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor. 4. Esomeprazole decreases the level or effect of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 5. Cenobamate reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Cenobamate increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Consider reducing the dose of CYP2C19 substrates when used concomitantly with cenobamate. 7. Esomeprazole increases the level or effect of citalopram by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. The maximum recommended dose of citalopram for patients taking CYP2C19 inhibitors is 20 mg/day due to the risk of QT prolongation. 8. Esomeprazole increases the level or effect of clobazam by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Dosage adjustment may be required as CYP2C19 inhibitors can increase exposure to N-desmethylclobazam, the active metabolite. 9. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of clozapine by influencing hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Cobicistat increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 11. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may reduce the solubility and bioavailability of crizotinib, though no formal studies have been conducted. 12. Crofelemer increases the levels of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Crofelemer may inhibit CYP3A4 at gut concentrations but is unlikely to inhibit systemically due to minimal absorption. 13. Prolonged use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), such as esomeprazole, may cause hypomagnesemia, increasing the risk of toxicity when co-administered with cyclosporine. Use caution and monitor. 14. Esomeprazole decreases the level or effect of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Drugs that alter upper GI tract pH, such as PPIs, H2-blockers, and antacids, may reduce dabrafenib solubility and bioavailability. 15. Dabrafenib reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Use an alternative if available. 16. Esomeprazole increases the level or effect of diazepam (buccal and intranasal forms) by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 17. Both dichlorphenamide and esomeprazole decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 18. Esomeprazole increases the toxicity of digoxin due to prolonged PPI use, which may cause hypomagnesemia and increase the risk of digoxin toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 19. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of duloxetine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 20. Efavirenz reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Elagolix increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. 22. Elagolix reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. 23. Esomeprazole decreases the level or effect of eltrombopag by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Esomeprazole increases the level or effect of escitalopram by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Eslicarbazepine acetate increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Esomeprazole increases the level or effect of etravirine by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, etravirine increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Fedratinib increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Adjust the dose of CYP2C19 substrates as necessary. 28. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 29. Fexinidazole increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 30. Fluconazole increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 32. Esomeprazole increases the level or effect of fosphenytoin by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, fosphenytoin reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Avoid co-administration of gefitinib with PPIs if possible. If PPI treatment is required, separate doses by 12 hours. 34. Esomeprazole increases the level or effect of glipizide and glyburide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 35. Iloperidone increases the levels of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 36. Esomeprazole increases the level or effect of imipramine by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 37. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of iron dextran complex and iron sucrose by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 38. Istradefylline increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed with 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 39. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir due to increased gastric pH. Use caution and monitor. Ledipasvir solubility decreases as pH increases. Proton pump inhibitor doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. 40. Lenacapavir increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 41. Letermovir increases the levels of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor is a strong CYP3A4 inducer and has the potential to induce CYP2C19 and both induce and inhibit P-gp. 43. Esomeprazole increases methotrexate levels by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor. There is an increased risk of toxicity with higher doses. 44. Esomeprazole reduces the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. The release of methylphenidate extended-release capsules (Ritalin LA) is pH-dependent, and co-administration of antacids or acid suppressants could alter its release. Consider separating the administration of antacids and methylphenidate extended-release capsules. 45. Mitotane reduces the levels of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 46. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. The potential interaction applies to mycophenolate mofetil. Enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium formulations are less sensitive to this interaction. The clinical significance is unclear. 47. Pentobarbital reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 48. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Esomeprazole increases the level or effect of phenytoin by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, phenytoin reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 50. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 51. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conversely, posaconazole increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 52. Primidone reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Rifampin reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Rifampin also reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 54. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of riociguat by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 55. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 56. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 57. Sparsentan reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Sparsentan, a CYP2C19 inducer, decreases the exposure of CYP2C19 substrates and reduces their efficacy. 58. St. John’s Wort reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 59. Stiripentol reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider reducing the dose of CYP2C19 substrates if adverse reactions occur when co-administered with stiripentol. 60. Esomeprazole increases the level or effect of tacrolimus by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Concomitant administration may increase tacrolimus whole blood concentrations, particularly in intermediate or poor metabolizers of CYP2C19. 61. Tazemetostat reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 62. Triclabendazole increases the level or effect of esomeprazole by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. If plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates are elevated during triclabendazole treatment, recheck plasma concentrations after discontinuation of triclabendazole. 63. Esomeprazole reduces the level or effect of vismodegib by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor.
